respondent:
Prem Prakesh Agarwal
Supreme Court of India

23 November 1993
The Judgment was delivered by : N. P. Singh, J.
1. One appeal on behalf of S.K. Saba and the other on behalf of the State of Madhya Pradesh, have been filed against the judgment of the High Court, directing to treat the appellant, junior to the writ petitioners/respondents in the cadre of Assistant Director of Industries.
2. The appellant was appointed as Foreman, Cycle Parts Factory, by the erstwhile Madhya Bharat Government, on October 31, 1956. The appointment was for one year on contract basis. The appellant joined on January 4, 1957, after the formation of the new State of Madhya Pradesh, on November 1, 1956. Subsequently, the contract service of the appellant was extended from time to time by the State Government. The post of Foreman was a Class-111 post (non- gazetted). The State Government by its order dated December 18, 1959 declared the post as Gazetted Class-11, w.e.f. January 16, 1959.
3. An advertisem
facts: The appellant was appointed as Foreman, Cycle Parts Factory, by the erstwhile Madhya Bharat Government, on October 31, 1956.
The appointment was for one year on contract basis.
The post of Foreman was a Class-111 post (non-gazetted).
The State Government by its order dated December 18, 1959 declared the post as Gazetted Class-11, w.e.f. January 16, 1959.
An advertisement was published in the year 1959 by the Madhya Pradesh Public Service Commission (hereinafter referred to as the 'Commission'), inviting applications for the post of Foreman Class-11.
The State Government by its order dated May 12, 1960 appointed the appellant on temporary basis till further orders, to the post of Foreman w.e.f. January 4, 1957.

Respondent 1, who was one of the writ petitioners, before the High Court, had been appointed as Assistant Director of Industries on February 18, 1959 on basis of a recommendation by the Commission, pursuant to an advertisement issued in the year 1958.

The posts of Foreman and Assistant Director of Industries are equivalent and it is not in dispute that if the order dated May 12, 1960 appointing the appellant w.e.f. January 4, 1957 is held to be valid, then the appellant although appointed on May 12, 1960 on basis of the recommendation of the Commission will rank senior to the said respondent, who had been appointed on February 18, 1959.

The High Court has pointed out that once the appointment of the appellant had been made by the process of direct recruitment, there was no occasion to reckon his seniority taking into consideration the period during which he served the State on contract basis for one year, which was being extended from time to time.
In about January 1964, the State Government decided to transfer the Cycle Parts Factory to Madhya Pradesh Udyog Nigam, a Government Corporation.
The persons working in the said factory including the appellant were given option either to opt for the service under the said Corporation or for being absorbed in any other department of the State.

In the year 1972, the appellant made a representation that he should be taken back in the service of the State Government and by an order dated June 19, 1972, the State Government appointed him as Assistant Director of Industries.
issues: What is the relevant date for fixing inter se seniority of entrants in the same cadre, either by the same process or by different processes of recruitment?
Whether the appointment of the appellant according to rules was made on basis of the recommendation of the Commission on May 12, 1960.

Whether the State Government could have appointed the appellant on May 12, 1960 w.e.f. January 4, 1957 from a date not only prior to the date of the recommendation made by the Commission but even prior to the date of the advertisement in respect of the said post.

Whether once the appointment is made to a post according to rules, the seniority of the person so appointed is to be counted from the date of his appointment and not with regard to the date of his confirmation.

Whether where the initial appointment is only ad hoc and not according to rules and made as a stopgap arrangement, the officiation in such post cannot be taken into account for considering the seniority.
petitioner_arguments: The State Government by its order dated May 12, 1960 appointed the appellant on temporary basis till further orders, to the post of Foreman w.e.f. January 4, 1957.

It was pointed out before the High Court, on behalf of the said respondents, that the order dated May 12, 1960 appointing the appellant as Foreman was on the basis of an advertisement issued In the year 1959 and recommendation made by the Commission thereafter.
As such on basis of the said recommendation, the appellant could not have been appointed w.e.f. January 4, 1957.

It was also pointed out that till January 15, 1959, the post of Foreman was a non-gazetted post and it is only on January 16, 1959, when by the government order dated December 18, 1959, the said post was made a gazetted one, necessitating appointment, on the basis of the recommendation of the Commission.

Respondent 1, who was one of the writ petitioners, before the High Court, had been appointed as Assistant Director of Industries on February 18, 1959 on basis of a recommendation by the Commission, pursuant to an advertisement issued in the year 1958.

So it was pointed out on his behalf that the order dated May 12, 1960 of the State Government, appointing the appellant with effect from a retrospective date i.e. January 4, 1957, directly affected his seniority, which was violative of Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution.
respondent_arguments: There is no dispute that the appointment of the appellant according to rules was made on basis of the recommendation of the Commission on May 12, 1960.

In this background, there was no occasion to take into consideration the period when the appellant was continuing on ad hoc basis, especially, during the period when the post itself was a non-gazetted post.

The High Court has rightly held that while appointing him on the basis of the recommendation of the Commission, the date of appointment could not have been ante-dated and made to be effective w.e.f. January 4, 1957.

This Court has repeatedly struck down and decried any attempt on the part of the appointing authority to give a notional seniority from a retrospective date, especially, when this process affects the seniority of those who have already entered into the service.
court_reasoning: The High Court has rightly held that while appointing him on the basis of the recommendation of the Commission, the date of appointment could not have been ante-dated and made to be effective w.e.f. January 4, 1957.

This Court has repeatedly struck down and decried any attempt on the part of the appointing authority to give a notional seniority from a retrospective date, especially, when this process affects the seniority of those who have already entered into the service.
The same view has been reiterated in the case of State of W.B. v. Aghore Nath Dey (1993) 3 SCC 371 : 1993 SCC (L & S) 783 :(1993) 24 ATC 932 1993 Indlaw SC 229.

Any officiating on the post when it was a non-gazetted post cannot be held to be a continuous officiating on the post so as to entitle the appellant to count that period towards his continuous officiating.
holding: The High Court has rightly held that while appointing him on the basis of the recommendation of the Commission, the date of appointment could not have been ante-dated and made to be effective w.e.f. January 4, 1957.
The State Government by its order dated May 12, 1960 appointed the appellant on temporary basis till further orders, to the post of Foreman w.e.f. January 4, 1957.
The appointment of the appellant according to rules was made on basis of the recommendation of the Commission on May 12, 1960.

The State Government could not have appointed the appellant on May 12, 1960 w.e.f. January 4, 1957 from a date not only prior to the date of the recommendation made by the Commission but even prior to the date of the advertisement in respect of the said post.
